The following is the statement of...1. Erich Jacobsohn.......................

at........6.30 p.m.....on the....31st of May....and interpreted by................................

We the undersigned

1. Erich Jacobsohn, 32 years,
s/(Teacher, Inter-) 343/14 Ward Road.

2. Timon Peismann, 41 years (Outfitter)
365/3 Tongshan Road, Married.

After issue of the Proclamation of 10.2.43 we approached
the Gendarmerie Canton Road regarding the possibility of
opening an office in order to assist people to do the necessary
formalities with the authorities concerned i.e. Stateless
Refugee Bureau and Gendarmerie.
To this effect we wrote a letter explaining our intention
which we handed to the Gendarmerie and to the Stateless Refugee
Bureau saying that it would be a help for the people who did
not know enough English or who did not want to go to the offices
themselves. At the same time we would make things easier for
the offices in filling in the necessary forms properly, thus
saving time and superfluous inquiries. Furthermore all our
clients did not have to go to Wei-hai-wei Road or Canton Road
and crowd these offices.

After having shown our letter and after having explained
orally we obtained a permission to advertise and opened an
office on the 17th of March in the Tabarin 1166 Broadway which
we rented from Mr. Willy Hirsch, At first only very few people
came to us as nobody moved yet then. For the first month our
expenses were about $300- for rent, advertising and office
material.

On April 28th we had to leave those premises as they were

exchanged and we settled down in the restaurant "Delibar"
Bubna Road. From then many people came to us to get the
permits as the time was getting short. We had to work very hard
to fill in the forms to go to Bubna Road, waiting for hours
to get the necessary chops. Then we had to fill in the papers
for Canton Road, make lists and bring the applications to
Gendarmerie. After some days we had to sort out our passes in
Canton Road which took two hours and more, and hand them to
the applicants.

For our services which included translations, writing of
contracts and interpretation, we charged our clients in the
beginning about $10.00, later $15.00 and $20.00 for each set,
some we did free of charge for poor people and friends whereas
others paid $10.00 more if more work was involved. In the
beginning of May we had to employ 2 assistants to fill in the
forms as most of our clients were very nervous and in a hurry so
that we could clear our cases every day and help people to get
their removal-passes in time.

As the idea originated from three partners we divided all
incoming money after deducting the costs between us three.

The total amount which every one of us got since we started
out work which was in the beginning of March was about $3,000
this means about $1,000.00 per month.

The third partner is Fred Tang, 777 Tongshan Road
Advertising single, 40 years.

Respectfully.
Erich Jacobsohn.
Simon Reismann.

UNIVERSUM.
SUBJECT: Advertisment appearing in the "Shanghai Jewish
"Chronicle" on the 17-3-1943

Inquiries conducted with regard to the attached advertisement elicited the following information.

The persons who organized the office are:

1. Simon Heissman, stateless refugee, age 40,
residing at 865/3 Tongshan Rd

2. Siegfried Lang, stateless refugee, age 41,
residing at 777 Tongshan Rd

3. Erich Jacobsohn, stateless refugee, age 32,
residing at 600/2 Ave. Haig F.C..

Simon Heissmann was formerly a salesman of the
Sphinx tie Factory. At present he has no occupation but he enjoys a good reputation in refugee circles. As a merchant he was not very successful in Shanghai.
Siegfried Lang is employed with the Shanghai
Jewish Chronicle as a canvasser for advertisements
He came to the notice of this Section during
1941 when he applied for entertainment licences
which he needed for concerts and floorshows,
arranged by him in various establishments in the
Wayside District. Nothing is known to his detriment.
Erich Jacobsohn was employed with an English family as a tutor until recently. On the Pao Chia
form he entered his profession as "Private Teacher". At present he is understood to give English lessons.

The manner in which the 3 above mentioned
proceeded before opening the office was as follows:

On March 5th, 1943 they sent a letter to Mr.
Kubota, in which they proposed to establish an office which
was to deal with formalities in connection with the removal of stateless refugees into the segregated area. In
this letter they furthermore pointed out that a great press
of work and many callers were to be expected and the existence of such an office would relieve the authorities
from much work. Mr. Kubota contacted Dr. A. J. Cohn, chairman
of the S.J.C.R.A., about the contents of the letter and
Dr. Cohn raised no objections. When Mr. Jacobsohn called

in person on Mr. Kubota in connection with the letter, he received verbal permission for the establishment of the Office. Before the attached advertisement was published it was shown to Mr. Kubota for approval. The sheet on which the advertisement was typed, bears a Japanese chop, said to be Mr. Kubota's, and the remark "Approved". This is the only written matter in their possession. Mr. Kubota also informed the the Japanese Gendarmerie Office at 94 Canton Rd, consequent to which Mr. Reissmann called there and received a bundle of application forms for removal permits. When the scheme will be working, stateless refugees may obtain forms from the "Universum" and hand them in there. The "Universum" will collect them and pass on to the Office at 94 Canton Rd.

Apart from this work the "Universum" will undertake interpreter services, writing of letters, negotiations on behalf of clients and other services in connection witht the removal for which they will charge moderate fees. These fees will have to cover expenses incurred by the running of the office and salaries for the 3 organizers.

The premises occupied by the office are the former "Tabarin" Bar and Restaurant. They are now empty except for a small desk. The monthly rent paid for them is $ 350.- per month. The name "Universum" is Latin .Its English translation is "Universe".
